To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elaborations that are specific and varied, whether generated by learners or authors, are more effective than elaborations that are either specific and constant or varied and constant for recall of conceptual knowledge.

1) the type of elaboration (learner-generated vs. author-generated) and elaboration specificity (specific elaborations vs. varied elaborations) interacted to produce differential effects on subjects’ ability recall, classify, identify, and apply the concepts, and 2) elaboration type and elaboration specificity did not interact to produce differential effects in terms of subjects’ ability to generate novel examples of the concepts.

elaboration type (learner-generated vs. author-generated) and elaboration specificity (specific vs. varied) interact to affect the recall, classification, and application of the concepts presented in prose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of elaborations on the acquisition of conceptual problem-solving skills from text.
the acquisition of conceptual knowledge and the role of elaborative activities in that acquisition process.
the acquisition of conceptual knowledge from prose and the role of elaborative activities in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
elaborations are effective for the acquisition of conceptual problem-solving skills.
elaboration is effective in promoting learning, but the type of elaboration is critical.
the effects of elaborative activities on conceptual learning are dependent upon a number of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the elaborative activities that we studied were not effective for improving the ability to recall, categorize, or transfer the concepts that subjects learned from the text.
elaborations that focus on the context of target concepts and that vary across concepts facilitate the acquisition of conceptual knowledge.
the effects of elaboration on the acquisition of conceptual knowledge are dependent on the type of elaboration, the type of knowledge, and the type of knowledge measure used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should encourage learners to engage in generative learning strategies that involve creating their own examples and definitions of concepts.
elaboration is a critical component to learning from text.
the more specific the elaboration, the better.
